question: According to the current NRP (2020) guidelines, a vigorous baby born through meconium-stained amniotic fluid should undergo immediate routine endotracheal intubation and suctioning before stimulation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false — an important evidence-based change. Routine intubation of vigorous MSAF babies is no longer recommended (NRP 2015/2020). Evidence showed it caused harm (laryngospasm, trauma) without benefit. Reserve intubation for non-vigorous babies only.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. The 2015/2020 NRP update REMOVED routine intubation and suctioning for vigorous babies (good tone, HR >100, crying) born through MSAF. Such babies receive routine care. Intubation for suctioning is now reserved for non-vigorous babies with depressed respiratory effort, poor tone, or HR <100 bpm.
